upstream.note: The revision every upstream citation below was read at, and the release docs/PARITY_GAP_ANALYSIS.md pins. github.com/tailscale/tailscale was cloned shallow at tag v1.102.4; HEAD was verified as bbcd7d1fc2054b9189ebc1531acf74bd880ca0c8.

summary.note: This edition audits the eight parity ports merged after the previous edition (#484, #497, #530, #531, #535, #538, #544, #547), each re-read diff by diff against github.com/tailscale/tailscale at v1.102.4. #497 and #531 were each listed twice (two review rounds); each has one row covering both. Divergences the original commit disclosed are still filed, because they still differ from the Go the diff cites, and each finding says whether it was disclosed. Each row's `divergences` lists the [pr-n] tags its findings carry.

auditedPrs.notes: Squash 84f399d. Read against cmd/tailscaled/tailscaled.go and feature/condregister/maybe_bird.go at v1.102.4 (bbcd7d1fc2054b9189ebc1531acf74bd880ca0c8). The commit cites 53a0d659; the bird guard, flag registration and check order are the same at both refs. Matches Go on exit 1, no log prefix, an empty path accepted, and refusing before --cleanup. Gaps: the flag is refused on every platform (no engine BIRD hook; disclosed), the message wording (disclosed), and the check now runs before the darwin root check (not disclosed). Findings: [484-1], [484-2], [484-3].

Squash 4dce9c2. Covers both review rounds of this PR. Verified: no mask bit, no diffing, and the initial notify filled only under NotifyInitialNetMap with SelfNode.Valid(). The claim that Go re-sends SelfChange on every netmap update is too broad. Go builds it only on the full-netmap path (setControlClientStatus); UpdateNetmapDelta sends no SelfChange. The merged code attaches self_change to every net_map frame, delta ticks included. Findings: [497-1], [497-2], [497-3], [497-4].

Squash a787db8. Matches Go on Apply as a three-state value and on set judging the prefs after the edit (editPrefsLocked: ApplyEdits then checkPrefsLocked). Diverges: the config file is refused at load where Go never checks it (disclosed), the refusal text is not Go's, and set stops at the first failure with routes checked before auto-update instead of joining every error. up does not check a stored opt-in (disclosed in QUESTIONS). Findings: [530-1], [530-2], [530-3], [530-4].

Squash a38687b. The four reason strings match tailcfg.CheckTag word for word, the 'tag: %q: %s' frame matches up.go, and so does the tag: completion. The claim that the refusal is byte-identical to Go's does not hold at the terminal: tnet up prepends 'error: ' where Go prints the bare error. The check also runs in the daemon and on set, neither of which upstream has (both disclosed in doc comments). Findings: [538-1], [538-2].

Squash a8b5fbf. The four refusals it re-frames print bare on stderr with exit 1, as cmd/tailscale/tailscale.go does. Leaving Go's literal 'Error: --service' strings unprefixed is also correct. Gaps: two of the new process tests pin outcomes Go never reaches, because Go makes daemon calls (GetServeConfig, status, verifyFunnelEnabled) before those refusals. A bad --accept-app-caps still exits 1 under anyhow framing, where Go's flag package exits 2. Findings: [544-1], [544-2], [544-3], [544-4].

Squash c872cca. The main fix is right: an interrupted listener or CGI run exits 0, and the pref is restored only on !cgi && startedManagementClient, as in Go. Gaps: Ctrl-C is only caught once serving starts, so a SIGINT during the pref step still exits 130 and can leave the pref on. The commit and doc comment claim Go-like early handling. Also, a CGI serve error exits 1 where Go logs it and exits 0 (this predates the commit). Findings: [547-1], [547-2], [547-3].

Squash 3977ad9. Covers both the review round and the audit round of this PR. Behaviour matches today: a frame is pushed only when the effective policy changed, store-then-tick, as in rsop reloadNow (Swap, then !old.EqualItems(new), then Invoke) and sysPolicyChangedForSession. One latent gap: change is judged on rendered string rows, not Go's typed raw-item hash. It cannot be observed while the only policy source is read once at startup. Findings: [531-1].

Squash ddd2fb8, which rewrote PARITY_AUDIT.json. Spot-checked rows #459, #466, #469, #472, #480 and #482 against bbcd7d1: their citations and claims are accurate. The #476 finding's example misstates upstream: Go exits 0 on that command line through flag.ErrHelp. The row also presents the missing verifyFunnelEnabled as undisclosed, though #476's own commit disclosed it. Findings: [535-1], [535-2].

gate.detail: Main at ba180be, toolchain 1.95.0 (the box's default nightly has no clippy; CI uses stable). fmt --check: pass. clippy --all-targets -D warnings: pass. cargo test --all-targets: run once with the session's long TMPDIR, it failed one test, tailnetd tests::cleanup_refuses_live_socket ('path must be shorter than SUN_LEN'): the socket path built under temp_dir() exceeds macOS's 104-byte sun_path. Rerun with --no-fail-fast and a short TMPDIR: every test passed, across 42 binaries, and that one passed too. tests/parity_audit_ledger.rs also passes against main's PARITY_AUDIT.json and against this one. cargo build --release --bins: pass. Pass is recorded because the only failure was the host's temp path; the test does depend on TMPDIR length.

findings.title: [497-1] self_change is sent on peer-delta frames, where Go sends no SelfChange
findings.detail: Upstream builds Notify.SelfChange only in setControlClientStatus, on a full netmap (if st.NetMap.SelfNode.Valid() { selfChange = st.NetMap.SelfNode.AsStruct() }). Patch, online and seen-time responses go through UpdateNetmapDelta, which sends a Notify with only the peer-change fields. In the merged code (src/server.rs, stream_notify), a fresh self report is fetched and attached to every frame that carries net_map, and the engine ticks net_map on liveness-only and patch-only deltas. So a watcher gets a 'self may have changed' signal on every peer online/offline flip. The rustdoc in src/localapi.rs repeats the claim that Go re-sends the self node with every netmap update. Not disclosed.

findings.title: [497-2] A netmap that changes only this node emits no self_change frame
findings.detail: Upstream: every full netmap, including one where only SelfNode changed (key expiry extended, rename, address change), sends a Notify with SelfChange. Merged: the engine bus ticks only on the peer watch, so a self-only change produces no frame and watchers never learn it. Disclosed, and tracked as an engine ask (docs/ENGINE_ASKS.md #46). The fix is engine-side.

findings.title: [497-3] SelfReport is a five-field subset, and its name has no trailing dot
findings.detail: Upstream: SelfChange is a full *tailcfg.Node (ipn/backend.go), including caps, tags and User, and Node.Name is the FQDN with a trailing dot. Merged: SelfReport carries stable_id, name, ipv4, ipv6 and key_expiry. Its name comes from the engine's display name, which has no trailing dot and falls back to the bare hostname. The subset is disclosed; the name-format difference is not.

findings.title: [497-4] self_change can go missing on a timeout, not only when self is invalid
findings.detail: Upstream: SelfChange is nil only when !SelfNode.Valid(), and it is taken from the same netmap that triggered the notify. Merged: fetch_self_report returns None after the 500 ms STATUS_QUERY_TIMEOUT or an engine error, even when a valid self exists. It is also fetched separately at frame time, so it can briefly disagree with the net_map in the same frame. The timeout path is disclosed.

findings.title: [530-1] A config-file AutoUpdate.Apply=true is refused at load; Go never checks it there
findings.detail: Upstream: initPrefsFromConfig and setConfigLocked (ReloadConfig) do p.ApplyEdits(&mp) and then SetPrefs/setPrefsLocked. Neither calls checkPrefsLocked, so a config-file opt-in is applied without checkAutoUpdatePrefsLocked. Merged: Config::apply_to_prefs (src/conffile.rs) runs selfupdate::check_auto_update_pref and bails with 'config: AutoUpdate.Apply: …'. The whole apply aborts, so the daemon will not start, or a reload fails, where Go carries on. Deliberate and disclosed in the commit, but a behavioural divergence from the code it cites.

findings.title: [530-2] The auto-update refusal text is not Go's sentence
findings.detail: Upstream checkAutoUpdatePrefsLocked returns errors.New("Auto-updates are not supported on this platform.") and nothing more. Merged (src/ipn/selfupdate.rs) renders '{reason}. Enabling auto-update would advertise Hostinfo.AllowsUpdate… {remedy}', with new REMEDY_CLI / REMEDY_CONFIG sentences. On a Homebrew install the opening reads '…not supported on this installation: …', so even Go's leading sentence is gone. Not disclosed as a departure from Go.

findings.title: [530-3] set reports only the first violation, routes first, instead of Go's joined errors
findings.detail: Upstream EditPrefs goes through checkPrefsLocked, which collects every violation and returns errors.Join(errs...), with checkAutoUpdatePrefsLocked before checkAdvertiseRoutes. Merged begin_set returns early at validate_advertise_routes(...)? (src/ipn/mod.rs ~3718) before reaching check_auto_update_pref (~3773). A set that breaks both rules reports only the route error. The commit's claim that set and check-prefs now agree, in Go's order, holds only for check_prefs. Not disclosed.

findings.title: [530-4] up never runs the auto-update check, unlike Go's startLocked
findings.detail: Upstream startLocked calls b.checkPrefsLocked(opts.UpdatePrefs), so up refuses an unhonourable auto-update opt-in. Merged begin_up does not call check_auto_update_pref. Disclosed in the commit's QUESTIONS section.

findings.title: [484-1] --bird-socket is refused on every platform; Go accepts it on linux/darwin/freebsd/openbsd
findings.detail: Upstream registers the flag when buildfeatures.HasBird. condregister/maybe_bird.go (//go:build !ts_omit_bird && (linux || darwin || freebsd || openbsd)) installs wgengine.HookNewBird, so a default build on those OSes accepts the path and passes it on as conf.BIRDSocket. Merged can_use_bird() (src/bin/tailnetd.rs) always returns Err, and tailnetd refuses any non-empty --bird-socket. Disclosed. The real fix is engine-side (no BIRD hook in tailscale-rs).

findings.title: [484-2] The bird refusal now runs before the darwin root check; Go runs it after
findings.detail: Upstream main checks, in order: the darwin requires-root refusal, then '--socket is required', then the --bird-socket guard. Merged tailnetd runs the bird refusal first, then the TPM refusals, then the darwin root check. A non-root macOS user who passes --bird-socket without userspace networking sees the bird line in tailnetd, where Go prints the root refusal. The code comment says only that the refusal comes 'before --cleanup'. The ordering is not disclosed.

findings.title: [484-3] The --bird-socket refusal's wording and framing differ from Go's bare log.Fatalf line
findings.detail: Upstream: log.SetFlags(0); log.Fatalf("--bird-socket is not supported on %s", runtime.GOOS). That is one bare line naming the GOOS, with no trailing full stop. Merged: 'error: --bird-socket is not supported on this platform or in this build of tailnetd.' followed by explanatory paragraphs. Go's sentence survives only as a substring. Disclosed in the doc comment.

findings.title: [547-1] SIGINT during web's pref step still exits 130 and can leave the pref on
findings.detail: Upstream runWeb installs signal.NotifyContext(ctx, os.Interrupt) as its first statement, so an interrupt during setRunWebClient either returns context canceled (exit 1) or reaches the shutdown goroutine, which restores the pref and exits 0. Merged (src/bin/tnet.rs) awaits start_tailscaled_web_client before tokio::signal::ctrl_c() is first polled in serve_until_interrupt. A SIGINT during the status/prefs/set calls kills the process with 130, and if it lands after the pref was set, the pref stays on. The commit and doc comment both say the handling matches Go's early install. Not disclosed.

findings.title: [547-2] web restores the pref while the listener still accepts; Go shuts the server down first
findings.detail: Upstream's interrupt goroutine calls webServer.Shutdown() before it logs 'stopping tailscaled web client' and calls setRunWebClient(false). Merged edits the pref before the serve future is dropped, so connections are still accepted during the restore. Disclosed.

findings.title: [547-3] A web --cgi serve error exits 1; Go logs it and exits 0
findings.detail: Upstream: if err := cgi.Serve(...); err != nil { log.Printf("tailscale.cgi: %v", err) } and then return nil, so the exit is 0. Merged run_web_cgi passes stdout write errors back to main, so the exit is 1. This predates the commit, but it is on the CGI exit path the commit re-wrapped and describes as Go-faithful.

findings.title: [538-1] tnet up prints 'error: ' before the tag refusal Go prints bare
findings.detail: Upstream cmd/tailscale/tailscale.go main does fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err), so the operator sees 'tag: "foo:bar": …' alone. Merged tnet up prints eprintln!("error: {message}") (src/bin/tnet.rs ~3983), so the line becomes 'error: tag: "foo:bar": …'. The commit says the refusal 'is now byte-identical to Go's'. That is true of the message, not of what reaches stderr. Not disclosed.

findings.title: [538-2] Tag validation runs in the daemon and on set; upstream checks tags only in up
findings.detail: Upstream checks and completes tags only in prefsFromUpArgs in cmd/tailscale/cli/up.go. checkPrefsLocked has no tag rule, and set.go has no --advertise-tags flag at this ref. Merged refuses bad tags in the daemon (src/ipn/mod.rs), so a LocalAPI client that Go would accept is refused here. It also completes a bare 'server' to 'tag:server' daemon-side and applies the Go-worded refusal to set. Predates the commit and is disclosed in doc comments.

findings.title: [544-1] The --tun refusal fires before any daemon call; a test pins that as Go's bytes
findings.detail: Upstream runServeCombined calls e.lc.GetServeConfig (wrapped 'error getting serve config: %w') and then getLocalClientStatusWithoutPeers ('getting client status: %w'). Only after those does it return errors.New("tun mode is only supported for services"). Merged refuses before contacting the socket. tests/serve_refusal_stderr_framing.rs runs this case against a socket that does not exist and asserts Go's sentence, where Go would print the connection or serve-config error. The ordering predates the commit, but the new test records it as parity.

findings.title: [544-2] funnel --proxy-protocol refuses without Go's earlier verifyFunnelEnabled
findings.detail: Upstream, for funnel, calls e.verifyFunnelEnabled(ctx, 443), a daemon round trip with its own refusals, before cleanURLPath and both PROXY-protocol checks. Merged has no verifyFunnelEnabled. The new test asserts that 'funnel --proxy-protocol=1 3000' prints the bare PROXY sentence with no daemon, where Go would fail at the funnel step first. The missing check predates the commit; the test now pins the non-Go order.

findings.title: [544-3] A bad --accept-app-caps exits 1 under anyhow framing; Go's flag package exits 2
findings.detail: Upstream builds the serve flag set with flag.ExitOnError. A bad value fails in acceptAppCapsFlag.Set, and the flag package prints 'invalid value … for flag -accept-app-caps: …' plus usage and exits 2. Merged parse_accept_app_caps(...)? (src/bin/tnet.rs) propagates through anyhow: an 'Error: serve via <socket>' header, 'Caused by:', exit 1. It sits in the same function the commit re-framed, before any daemon call. Only partly disclosed (QUESTIONS covers the 'via <socket>' wrapper, not the exit code).

findings.title: [544-4] The two --service refusals still print under anyhow's 'serve via' wrapper
findings.detail: Upstream returns errors.New("Error: --service flag is not supported with funnel") (and its sibling), which main prints as one bare line, exit 1. Merged still prints them under 'Error: serve via <socket>' / 'Caused by:'. Disclosed in the commit's QUESTIONS section and pinned by a test.

findings.title: [535-1] The #476 finding's example misstates upstream: Go exits 0 on that command line
findings.detail: The audit row says 'tnet funnel --set-path=/a/../b --https=70000' is refused upstream 'first with the funnel capability error'. That command line has no target. Go's validateArgs runs before verifyFunnelEnabled and returns flag.ErrHelp when len(args) == 0, and cli.go maps flag.ErrHelp to nil, so Go exits 0 without reaching the funnel, mount-point or port checks. The underlying divergence (no verifyFunnelEnabled port) is real; the example is wrong.

findings.title: [535-2] The #476 row presents the missing verifyFunnelEnabled as undisclosed
findings.detail: Upstream runServeCombined calls verifyFunnelEnabled between the two --service refusals, and the audit row is right that it has no counterpart. But #476's own commit says Go's verifyFunnelEnabled has no counterpart and none was added. The row and finding omit that, unlike the #466, #469, #472 and #480 rows, which record disclosure.

findings.title: [531-1] Policy change is judged on rendered string rows, not Go's typed raw-item hash
findings.detail: Upstream reloadNow invokes change callbacks only when !old.EqualItems(new). EqualItems compares a deephash over the raw items (Value, Error, Origin), so it is type-aware and sees every value. Merged reload_and_publish (src/ipn/syspolicy.rs) compares Vec<PolicySetting> display rows, where values are %v-rendered and AuthKey is shown as '<redacted>'. Two values that differ only in type, or an AuthKey-only change, would compare equal and push no frame. Cannot be observed today, because the only policy source is read once at startup. It would surface as soon as a store re-reads. AuthKey redaction is disclosed; losing the type is not.
